title: Worldbuilding deep dives
description: Bigger worlds and longer arcs for listeners who want systems, history, and scope.
label: Big worlds

showReasons.midnight-burger: Its cosmic premise keeps opening into more places and people.
showReasons.vast-horizon: A large sci-fi setting gives the world scale quickly.
showReasons.ars-paradoxica: Its time-science structure builds a dense alternate-history frame.
showReasons.impact-winter: A cinematic survival world with enough lore to keep expanding.
showReasons.the-waystation: A wormhole waystation and the investigation of its destruction give it a compact cosmic-horror setting.
showReasons.were-alive: A long survival saga with room for factions, geography, and consequence.
showReasons.midst: A stranger, more formally ambitious worldbuilding story for listeners who want the cosmos to feel authored all the way down.
showReasons.marsfall: The colony politics and systems pressure give the collection another lived-in frontier world.
showReasons.the-strange-case-of-starship-iris: Resistance politics and ensemble space-opera sprawl deepen the social worldbuilding.
showReasons.tumanbay: A city-scale political world that keeps expanding through pressure and perspective.
showReasons.the-once-and-future-nerd: Portal fantasy that earns its scale through social and political detail.
showReasons.flash-gordon-and-buck-rogers-radio-adven: The vintage serials offer a direct look at the planetary adventure worlds that shaped later space opera.
